requestedActions.title: Read issue titles in the connected person's workspace, including pagination

guide.summary: Read issue titles through Linear's GraphQL API using an OAuth user-account token from each connected customer. The documented default read grant covers this, and the write scopes are excluded. Customer distribution approval is not established by the supplied sources.
guide.recommendation: The requested access is documented. Follow the saved setup steps and run each representative API test; execution has not been verified.
guide.nextAction: Create the OAuth application in Linear settings

findings.title: OAuth2 is documented for building applications that integrate with Linear
findings.detail: Linear documents OAuth2 as the recommended approach for applications that integrate with Linear, and the GraphQL API accepts OAuth access tokens as a Bearer header.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to the third-party app connecting each customer account through OAuth.

evidence.quote: Linear supports OAuth2 authentication, which is recommended if you’re building applications to integrate with Linear.
### OAuth If you’re building an application for others to use, we recommend you use OAuth2 authentication. Once you complete the authentication flow and acquire an access token, pass it

findings.title: Request the read scope for the connected user account
findings.detail: The documented read scope is the default read access for the user's account and is always present, so it is the grant to request for reading issue titles.

evidence.quote: * `read` - (Default) Read access for the user's account. This scope will always be present.

findings.title: OAuth read grant is broader than issue titles
findings.detail: Linear documents read as account-wide read access, so the token can read more than issue titles. The app cannot narrow it to read-only by claiming application restrictions; this is a provider limitation to disclose.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to the OAuth access token for each connected customer.

evidence.quote: * `read` - (Default) Read access for the user's account. This scope will always be present.
### OAuth If you’re building an application for others to use, we recommend you use OAuth2 authentication. Once you complete the authentication flow and acquire an access token, pass it

findings.title: Do not request write or issue-mutation scopes
findings.detail: The issues:create scope allows creating and updating issues, which conflicts with the stated prohibitions. The write scope is also broader than needed. Neither is requested for this read-only feature.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to scope selection for this app.

evidence.quote: * `issues:create` - Allows creating and updating issues, and creating their attachments
* `write` - Write access for the user's account. If your application only needs to create comments, use a more targeted scope

findings.title: Cursor pagination uses first, after and pageInfo
findings.detail: Results are paginated with first and after arguments. Continue while pageInfo.hasNextPage is true, passing pageInfo.endCursor as after.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to the issue-title listing across all pages.

evidence.quote: } ``` To query the next 10, simply pass the value of `pageInfo.endCursor` as `after` parameter for the next request. You can do this as long as `pageInfo.hasNextPage` return true
issues(first: 10) { edges {
hasNextPage endCursor } }

findings.title: Admin requirement applies only to app-actor installs
findings.detail: The supplied guidance says admin permissions are required for actor=app workspace installs. This does not apply to a user-actor OAuth token from an individual customer account.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies only if the app is changed to the app actor model.

evidence.quote: to an app installation rather than requesting authentication as the installing user. Because this will be installed with a workspace scope _admin permissions are required_ to complete the installation.

steps.title: Create the OAuth application in Linear settings
steps.detail: Create the OAuth application in a workspace set aside for managing it, since each admin will have access. Record the client ID and secret and configure the redirect URL used by the callback.
steps.doneWhen: OAuth application exists and its client ID, client secret and redirect URL are saved.

evidence.quote: > [!NOTE] > It is **highly recommended** you create a workspace for the purpose of managing the OAuth2 Application, as each admin user will have access.
`state` | (optional, **recommended**) Prevents CSRF attacks and should always be supplied. Read more about it here.

steps.title: Authorize a test customer account with read scope
steps.detail: Implement the callback and token exchange, then run the authorization URL with scope=read and a state value. Exchange the code for a token using client_id and client_secret. Authorization is setup, not a resource action.
steps.doneWhen: An access token for the representative test account is obtained and stored for the test.

evidence.quote: ### Example ```http GET https://linear.app/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=YOUR_REDIRECT_URL&state=SECURE_RANDOM&scope=read HTTP/1.1
1. Use HTTP basic authentication by passing a Base64-encoded `client_id:client_secret` string as an authorization header: `Authorization: Basic <base64(client_id:client_secret)>`
`state` | (optional, **recommended**) Prevents CSRF attacks and should always be supplied. Read more about it here.

steps.title: Read the first page of issue titles
steps.detail: Send the issues query with first: 10 from the connected test account and read id and title from each node, along with pageInfo hasNextPage and endCursor. Representative input: the test account OAuth access token. Expected result: a successful response containing issue edges with node title values and a pageInfo object. Boundary check: send only this query operation, make no mutation or write requests, and confirm in the request log that no create, update or delete request was sent.
steps.doneWhen: The first page returns issue titles and pageInfo fields for the test account, and the request log shows no write operations.

evidence.quote: issues(first: 10) { edges {
hasNextPage endCursor } }
--data '{ "query": "{ issues { nodes { id title } } }" }' \

request.example: curl '-X' 'POST' 'https://api.linear.app/graphql' '-H' 'Content-Type: application/json' '-H' 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>' '--data' '{"query":"query Issues { issues(first: 10) { edges { node { id title } cursor } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }"}'

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN from the test account authorization

steps.title: Optional: check directory listing for other-workspace distribution
steps.detail: Optional for direct installs and independent testing. Read the integration directory requirements only if the app will be made available to other workspaces. Verify whether a user-actor OAuth app needs review before customer rollout.
steps.doneWhen: Documented directory and review requirements for user-actor customer installs are confirmed or recorded as unresolved.

evidence.quote: You can build agents for internal use within your own workspace or for distribution to other organizations. It does not cost anything to develop agents in Linear. To make your
agent available to other workspaces, submit your agent to Linear's integration directory.

steps.title: Read the next page of issue titles
steps.detail: Repeat the same read-only query with the pageInfo.endCursor from the previous response passed as the after variable. Representative input: the test account access token and the endCursor string. Expected result: the next page of issue edges and pageInfo. Continue repeating while pageInfo.hasNextPage is true and stop when it is false, which is the documented end of the collection. Boundary check: send only read queries and confirm the request log contains no mutations.
steps.doneWhen: All pages are read until pageInfo.hasNextPage is false, with no mutations sent.

evidence.quote: } ``` To query the next 10, simply pass the value of `pageInfo.endCursor` as `after` parameter for the next request. You can do this as long as `pageInfo.hasNextPage` return true
hasNextPage endCursor } }

request.example: curl '-X' 'POST' 'https://api.linear.app/graphql' '-H' 'Content-Type: application/json' '-H' 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>' '--data' '{"query":"query Issues($after: String) { issues(first: 10, after: $after) { edges { node { id title } cursor } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }","variables":{"after":"<endCursor>"}}'

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN from the test account authorization
endCursor from the previous page response
